key_terms.الأئمة: The Imams — the rightful leaders of the Muslim community from the Prophet's household
key_terms.خلفاء الله: Caliphs of God — divine vicegerents appointed by God to govern His creation on earth
key_terms.عزّ وجلّ: Mighty and Majestic — a formula of divine glorification used with the name of God

ai.seo_question: Are the Imams the caliphs of God on earth according to Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him), the eighth Imam, declared that the Imams are the caliphs — the divinely-appointed vicegerents — of God on earth. This statement asserts the doctrine of Imamate as a continuation of God's governance over creation, analogous to Adam's designation as khalifah (vicegerent) in the Quran (2:30). In the early Abbasid context, this was a profound theological and political claim, asserting that authority over the Muslim community rightfully belongs to the Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt rather than to the ruling caliphs.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Abu Masoud, from Al Ja’fary who said,
‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The Imams<sup>asws</sup> are the Caliphs of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic in His<sup>azwj</sup> earth’.
en.sarwar: 1. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash‘ari has narrated from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from abu Mas‘ud from al-Ja’fari who has said that he heard abu al-Hassan al-Rida (a.s.) say the following. “
The Imams (a.s.) are the deputies of Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, on earth.”
